newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT, CRICKET - England's Stewart heads towards century.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT, CRICKET - England's Stewart heads towards century.

text.p: Alec Stewart was on target to score the first century of England's tour on Tuesday before rain interrupted the second day's play against a New Zealand Selection XI.
England had added 47 runs from 14.3 overs and moved to 153 for three in reply to the NZ Selection's 138 all out.

Stewart started the day on 40, with England at 106 for three. Partnered by vice-captain Nasser Hussain, he pushed England into a first-innings lead with an unbroken 49-run partnership for the fourth wicket before the rain came down.
Stewart had moved to 75 while Hussain was on 11.
Despite overnight rain, play began on time but dark clouds started gathered shortly after the start. Lightning flashed and thunder reverberated around the ground.
However Stewart, the top test run-scorer in 1996, didn't put a foot wrong in the first hour.
He displayed tidy defence and, when the chance arose, he punished anything loose to move to his 50 with fours in consecutive balls from medium pacer Justin Vaughan.
It had taken him 94 balls and included seven boundaries.
That over produced 11 runs and when fast-medium Danny Morrison came on for the seventh over of the day, he twice dropped the ball short and Stewart hooked and pulled him expertly to the fence.
Hussain had a tentative start, edging Vaughan just short of Craig Spearman at second slip before he had scored in the second over of the day.
He got moving by cutting the next ball to the backward point boundary. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746
